newsitem.title: POLAND: NFIs seen driving Warsaw stock market next week.
newsitem.headline: NFIs seen driving Warsaw stock market next week.

text.p: Players on the Warsaw bourse will focus next week on the difficult-to-valuate stocks of the National Investment Funds (NFI), in trade since Thursday, and may neglect other papers in near-term, analysts said on Friday.
Analysts said the NFIs of Poland's mass privatisation scheme gave short-term investors a profit opportunity, of which they have been deprived during the 13-week-long horizontal trend on the bourse.
"It's an ideal instrument for speculators who waited for something to happen, which would let them make some money," said Roman Sosnowski of WBK AIB Asset Management.
Analysts said, however, the high NFI volumes, which amounted to 69.7 million zlotys on Friday, signalled that long-term investors were also buying the stocks.

They said strong buying after price fixing on NFIs suggested the papers would extend their gains, although some analysts thought their growth was likely to slow down after the funds index NIF jumped 6.4 percent on Friday.
But they said most rational ways of valuating the funds were useless, because their 1996 earnings were significantly lowered by accounting operations.
Setting resistances for the NFIs is therefore impossible, they said. "A valuation of the funds is almost impossible," said Czeslaw Pospieszynski, an analyst at PBI brokerage.
The WIG index rose three percent to 16,482.1 points this week.
Analysts said that significant falls were unlikely next week even though the overall market was additionally under pressure from the current large privatisations.
"Some may sell to buy the NFIs and the market might be cooled but I don't think falls are likely as the market is not overvalued," Sosnowski said.
The stocks were trading at average 16.3 times historic earnings.
Bank Handlowy's public offering for individual investors ends on Friday, but investors will have their funds frozen at least until the shares are allotted at a special bourse session on June 21.
Analysts said investors would also generate funds for the copper concern KGHM's offering due to begin on June 30, worth at least 300 million zlotys.

Companies are due to report monthly earnings for May next week, but analysts said they were unlikely to have significant impact on the overall market. However, in some cases sharp moves up or down in reaction to the earnings are likely, they said.
Confectioner Mieszko starts bourse trade on Tuesday on the parallel market.
